'''''Lamarckia''''' is a genus of plants in the [[Poaceae|grass family]] native to the Old World Dry Belt, on the [[Mediterranean Region]], the Arabian Peninsula, East Africa and [[South Asia]]. It has a single species, '''''Lamarckia aurea''''', known colloquially as the '''golden dog's-tail'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''goldentop grass'''.<ref>{{PLANTS|id=LAAU|taxon=Lamarckia aurea|accessdate=23 January 2016}}</ref>

==Description==
It is an [[annual plant]], typically 30-45 centimetres in height, with clusters of golden [[flower]]s in a [[panicle]] 5–8 cm long and 2–2.5 cm broad.<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/417081#page/207/mode/1up Moench, Conrad. 1794.  Methodus Plantas Horti Botanici et Agri Marburgensis : a staminum situ describendi 201] in Latin</ref>

==Distribution==
The species is native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]] and neighboring regions from [[Portugal]] to the [[Canary Islands]] east to [[Ethiopia]] and northern [[India]]. It is also naturalized in parts of Australia and the Americas, considered an invasive weed in some areas.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lamarckia aurea (L.) Moench {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:406803-1 |website=Plants of the World Online |access-date=20 July 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
